summary: The goal is to show how the FastLanes layout spec works under the hood, share actual benchmark numbers, and start a discussion on what we might want to adopt. While other hardware configurations [Kosta's super laptop] show larger single-core gains, our multi-core tests suggest these advantages can shrink when multiple CPUs compete for memory bandwidth. But when measured against the highly optimized code Parquet (xsimd c++) already ships today, the actual margins shrink significantly, giving us a more realistic picture of the gains. Since the earlier PFOR thread I have kept measuring and improved decoding speed significantly, added a delta mode, and evaluated the encoding on real dictionary index runs.
